text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock has fallen about 4.6% over the past week, with today's small decline continuing a downward trend that accelerated sharply on October 21-22. The timing aligns with escalating Middle East tensions—Iran war threats and Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure sent Brent crude to six-month highs around $116—but paradoxically, refiners typically benefit when oil prices rise because they buy crude cheap and sell refined products at higher prices. The stock's weakness suggests the market is pricing in something beyond simple oil price moves, possibly concern that geopolitical disruption to crude supply chains or refining operations will outweigh margin gains, or that the current 93.4% refinery utilization rate has limited room to expand profitably.

The broader energy trade has rotated away from refiners and toward oil producers and liquefied natural gas exporters, which benefit more directly from higher crude prices without the operational complexity refiners face during supply shocks. With oil storage relatively high at 695 million barrels and gasoline in storage elevated, there's less urgency for refiners to run harder, which may be dampening investor enthusiasm for the sector despite headline oil prices hitting their highest levels in months.
